analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: TMT Earning Beats are not Being Rewarded, HF Performance and Positioning in October, The Fed as a Driver of Long Term Rates, Apple Disappoints, Previewing the Midterm Elections, Sector Sentiment Trends (3 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y with 60% of companies reported. That matches Q2 but ends the acceleration seen in Q1 and Q2. Median stock EPS growth slowed to 12% from 14%.
GIR expects about 30% EPS growth in 2026 and 18% in 2027, excluding non-recurring items.
Stocks that beat EPS estimates outperformed the S&P 500 by 152bp the day after reporting, above the historical median. TMT beats have generally gone unrewarded.

Estimate upgrades are slowing. Consensus 2027 EPS is up 2% since the season began. Analysts have cut margin estimates as energy prices rise. 60% of companies beat by more than one standard deviation, vs a 50% historical average and a 64% average over the past four quarters.

Hyperscaler capex is on track for about $800bn in 2026 (+96%) and is expected to reach $1.2tn in 2027 (+44%), with little revision this season. AI infrastructure EPS growth is expected to peak at 80% this quarter and slow to about 40% by late 2027.

Hyperscalers reported combined negative free cash flow of -$31bn in Q3. Cloud revenue for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT grew 54% y/y and is still accelerating, but crowded positioning set a high bar and results raised concern about AI disrupting other businesses' revenues.

Market breadth is widening. Since the season began 70% of S&P 500 stocks are up but they make up only 50% of index market cap. The index is down 3% while the S&P 500 ex-AI is up 5%. Energy prices and interest rates are the key determinants of whether non-tech can keep rising.
October hedge fund performance: Fundamental L/S -3.5% and Systematic L/S -3.6%, the first time on GS record (since 2016) both cohorts fell 3% or more.

Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, split equally between short and long sales. Net leverage fell at the fastest pace since March while gross leverage rose on mark-to-market. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell, led by Asia L/S funds.

Every region except DM Asia was net sold, led by EM Asia and North America. In US sectors, HFs rotated out of TMT and Cyclicals into Defensives. Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June. Defensives were net bought for the first time in 7 months, with Staples and Health Care net bought.

GS argues the latest rise in forward rates came with the Fed's shift to a new hiking cycle, not structural neutral-rate drivers or major macro events. GS thinks the conflict between the Fed-driven and deficit-plus-AI-financing explanations is overstated.

GS says persistent fiscal support and rising AI investment demand are likely reasons the economy has needed a higher rate structure. The market updates its pricing of those forces mainly through shifts in actual Fed policy ranges.

AAPL fell 4% pre-market after earnings as investors focused on memory costs hitting gross margin. December-quarter gross margin is guided to 45%-46%, a ~140bp sequential decline. CEO John Ternus called memory pricing 'unprecedented'.

AAPL Services growth of ~10% in Q4 is expected to slow to 8%-9% in December, below ~12% consensus growth, on FX, App Store regulatory pressure and weaker Google search-related payments. China sales fell nearly $1B short of estimates.
PLTR fell 8% after guiding a slowdown in bookings growth. AMD and Arista report today, giving reads on accelerator demand and hyperscaler networking spend after Intel and the optical sell-off.

Midterms: prediction markets imply high odds Democrats win the House with a wider margin. The Senate looks closer. Democrats lead polls in all Senate seats they defend, though two are within the margin of error.

Under a Democratic majority, fiscal deadlines are the main legislative focus. Spending authority expires Dec. 11 and the debt limit will need to be raised. Reversing last year's spending cuts would add an estimated 0.25% of GDP to 2027 spending.

GS expects new tariff increases from President Trump after the election that would more than offset tariff reductions, raising the US effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp. A national data center tax incentive moratorium looks unlikely. GS sees a possible compromise on basic federal AI oversight, with restrictive AI regulation unlikely.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT grew 54% y/y and is still accelerating. Hyperscaler capex is on track for about $800bn in 2026 (+96%) and $1.2tn in 2027 (+44%).
tension_points.bear_case: TMT beats are not being rewarded because crowded positioning set a high bar. AI capex growth looks to be peaking, AI infrastructure EPS growth slows from 80% to about 40% by late 2027, and hyperscaler combined free cash flow was -$31bn.

tension_points.theme: Fed versus structural drivers of rates
tension_points.bull_case: The Fed's shift to a new hiking cycle drove the latest rise in forward rates, not structural drivers.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal support and AI investment demand likely explain why the economy needs a higher rate structure, so the two explanations are not in conflict.
